body.statement: For every post period \(t\in\{T_0+1,\ldots,T_0+T_1\}\), the exact stable-span definitions have the following reductions. If \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell\), then \(E_{t,\ell}=m_\ell^{-1/2}\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\). If the treated intervention law \(F^I_{0t,\ell}\) and every donor law \(F_{jt,\ell}\), \(1\leq j\leq J\), are point masses, then \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}=0\) and \(E_{t,\ell}=A_{t,\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)=n_\ell^{-1}A_{t,\ell}(\sqrt{n_\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell))\). Thus known weights leave only the finite-support empirical-quantile error, point-mass post laws leave only the learned-weight quadratic, and imposing both conditions makes \(E_{t,\ell}=0\).
body.justification: These two exact reductions audit that the endpoint and weight components correspond to the intended post-treatment counterfactual estimand.
body.gap: The reductions are internal coherence checks rather than separate novelty claims; they connect the compound expansion to the fixed-weight discrete law and the standard tangent-cone quadratic special cases.
body.consumer: They give referees and the Zhai et al. reanalysis immediate falsification checks for implementations with known weights or degenerate post cells.
